LOCAL ENTERPRISE OFFICE WICKLOW CLIENTS CREATED OVER 115 JOBS IN 2025 
NOW SUPPORTING OVER 159 SMALL BUSINESSES AND 695 JOBS ACCORDING TO NEW FIGURES 
The annual results of the Local Enterprise Offices (LEOs) for 2025, were announced, which showed that 
companies supported by Wicklow County Council’s Local Enterprise Office created 115 jobs, in 2025.  
Net figures of 50 jobs were created by clients that the Local Enterprise Office supported in 2025. This 
takes into account companies that amalgamated, ceased trading and those that transferred onto 
Enterprise Ireland. The new figures show that the LEO Wicklow financially supported 159 small 
businesses in their portfolio across the county, and these companies in turn employ 695 people.  
The Local Enterprise Offices were to the fore in supporting small businesses across the country in 2025, 
helping thousands to secure funding, upskill and avail of supports to becoming more sustainable and 
competitive.  Recent supports such as the Grow Digital Voucher enables small businesses to take their 
first steps in digitalisation and the Market Explorer Grant supports companies in looking at new 
markets.  
The Local Enterprise Offices, funded through Enterprise Ireland, support thousands of small Irish 
businesses and entrepreneurs nationwide. Since their establishment in 2014 they have been the first 
stop shop for entrepreneurs and small businesses and providing a range of supports including financial, 
mentoring, training and sector specific expertise to help guide businesses at any stage of their 
development.  
They also run key initiatives to foster entrepreneurship across the country including Local Enterprise 
Week, National Women’s Enterprise Day, the Student Enterprise Programme and the National 
Enterprise Awards.  The Local Enterprise Offices are also running a campaign encouraging small 
businesses to save time money and energy by availing of their competitiveness and productivity 
supports including Green, Lean and Digital for Business.  www.AllInADaysWork.ie 
For more information on the Local Enterprise Offices go to www.LocalEnterprise.ie

Housing Needs Assessment 2024 (SSHA 2024) 
 
The Summary Social Housing Assessment (SSHA) 2024 is the continuation of the ongoing process of annual 
assessments of national housing need. It provides vital data to inform the ongoing development of housing policy. 
The purpose of the process is to identify the current level of national housing need. At county level, it captures the 
total number of households qualified for social housing support across the county whose social housing need is not 
being met, in order to understand the level of need for such support. The social housing applications were reviewed 
from 1st November 2023 to 4
thNovember 2024. The data on the housing needs for Wicklow was returned to the 
Department by 2
ndDecember 2024.

Capital Assistance Scheme (CAS) 
Under CAS, the Department is accepting applications for capital funding for the delivery, through either 
construction or acquisition, of housing accommodation, to cater for priority groups including: 
• 
elderly. 
• 
homeless persons (including “care leavers” exiting State care on reaching the age of 18). 
• 
people with a disability, with particular emphasis on moving people with disabilities from 
congregated settings into community-based living. 
 
Assessment criteria 
CAS funding operates in partnership with Local Authorities and Approved Housing Bodies.  
Local Authorities assess the specific need for CAS funded housing being cognisant of the actual housing 
need of the CAS groups identified in the latest Social Housing Assessment, consultations with suitable local 
inter-agency/co-ordination groups that deal with special needs, such as the housing and disability steering 
groups, national policies and guidelines, including the National Housing Strategy for Disabled People. 
To date, December 2025, Wicklow worked in partnership with Ark Housing and Tiglin to deliver on two 
properties in 2025.  Wicklow continues to work with Sunbeam House Services, Oaklee and National 
Association of Housing for Visually Impaired to bring active projects to completion.

Addressing Homelessness in Partnership with Approved Housing Bodies 
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – Kilmantin Hill, Wicklow 
Kilmantin Hill has 11 rooms to support persons either homeless, exiting a higher support facility, or in danger 
of becoming homeless.  
There are 9 clients supported in the Kilmantin Hill facility, operated by Dublin Simon. There is continuous 
transition by the clients to suitable alternative accommodation. 
A report is being undertaken at present to cost the refurbishment of the current rooms with a view to making 
them all ensuite. More details will be available over the coming months. 
 
Homeless Family Service – Fitzwilliam Road, Wicklow   
Dublin Simon are engaged by Wicklow County Council to operate and manage the facility at Fitzwilliam 
Road, Wicklow as a Family Homeless Service. The building comprises of three 1-bed units, two 2-bed units, 
and two 3-bed units. Eleven families have now transitioned or are in the process of transitioning to a 
permanent home and the resulting vacancies are in the process of being occupied with families 
experiencing or in danger of homelessness. 
It is envisaged that families will avail of the service for circa 6-months STA (Supported Temporary 
Accommodation) with key working support to enable families to transition from homelessness into 
Homeless HAP, or alternative longer-term accommodation.   
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – San Remo, Bray 
San Remo is operated by Dublin Simon and incorporates a service model whereby there are a number of 
emergency/cold weather initiative beds and Supported Temporary Accommodation Beds (STA). There is 
on site key working support linking in with clients.    
The Neighbourhood Liaison Committee is now operational and meets monthly. 
Bi-monthly meetings are held with Dublin Simon and Wicklow County Council staff. 
 
Homeless Supported Accommodation - Carraig Eden, Greystones 
This facility provides 35 ensuite bedrooms with associated kitchens and common areas and is fully 
operational. Wicklow County Council run an in-reach service with the clients to support them as they 
continue their journey into more permanent accommodation.  
 
Other Homeless Supported Accommodation 
Wicklow County Council owned properties in Wicklow, Bray, and Greystones, leased to Approved Housing 
Bodies, provide 12 units of low to medium supported accommodation targeted to the particular support 
needs of the clients. Six of these persons living in shared accommodation have now successfully moved 
into their forever homes and this in turn created space to move further people out of homelessness.  
A homeless outreach service has been rolled out in Bray and is proving very successful.

Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht, Dara Calleary TD, and Minister of State 
with responsibility for Community Development and Charities, Jerry Buttimer TD announced funding under 
the Department of Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht’s Local Enhancement 
Programme (LEP) 2026. 
This funding will provide capital supports that are essential for many small community groups and 
organisations, particularly those who serve disadvantaged communities in rural and urban areas. 
There will be a particular focus on small capital works/improvements, and the purchase of equipment for 
community use. The funding may be used for, but it is not limited to; improving access for persons with a 
disability; enhancing community participation for disadvantaged and marginalised groups and improving 
energy efficiency of community facilities to reduce ongoing costs. 
The scheme is designed to ensure local priorities are identified and met, to improve and enhance 
community facilities for all. Funding will be available to a diverse range of community groups including, but 
not limited to, community centres, parish halls and local voluntary groups. 
 
The LEP funding is about helping our communities, local groups and clubs. This funding will empower our 
communities to become even more vital hubs for activities and services.

Healthy Age Friendly Homes Programme Update: 
The Healthy Age Friendly Homes Programme in Wicklow continues to support older people, over 65 years 
of age, to live in their home for as long as possible.  
The Programme accepts referrals from a variety of sources including from: 
- 
The older person themselves 
- Local Authority Staff 
- 
Family and friends 
 
- Public Health Nurses, GP’s and Occupational Therapists   
- 
Elected Representatives 
 
- Community Organisations 
Please note, consent from the older person (verbal) must be obtained before the referral is submitted. 
Once the referral is received, the Local Coordinator will be in-touch with the older person to arrange a 
free home visit.

Since the commencement of the Healthy Age Friendly Homes Programme in Wicklow, in January 2024, 
the level of interest in the programme has been greater than anticipated. Consequently, a large number of

offers a wide range of supports to our participants, including but not limited to, arranging fall detector 
personal alarms, helping with housing adaptation grants, organising Care and Repair services, linking-in 
with community services, signposting the older person to health services etc.  
 
The programme has gone from strength-to-strength in Wicklow since its inception. The 2024 projected 
targets for the programme in Wicklow have been exceeded, which demonstrates the success of the

The Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant is a payment you can get if you are turning a vacant house or building into 
your permanent home or a rental property.  The grant applies to qualifying vacant properties in cities, towns, villages and 
rural parts of the country. 
There are 2 types of Grants available: 
• 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant of up to €50,000 
• 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant including the Derelict Property top up grant of up €70,000 
 
To qualify for the top up of €20,000, an independent report prepared by a Structural Engineer, along with a copy of their 
Professional Indemnity Insurance, is required to be submitted along with the application, confirming, to the satisfaction of 
the local authority, that the property is derelict i.e. structurally unsound and dangerous. 
To qualify for the grant, applicants must: 
Have proof of ownership or evidence of active negotiations to buy the property (that is, confirmation of engagement from 
the estate agent or owner of the property) where you are seeking approval in principle for a grant. 
- 
Live in the property as your principal private residence or make it available for rent. 
- 
Have proof that the property has been vacant for at least 2 years and that it was built up to and including 2007.

GIS & Systems Analysis 
 
1. Residential Zoned Land Tax (RZLT) Mapping 
Significant progress has been made on the preparation of the Residential Zoned Land Tax maps for 2026 and 2027. 
Updated mapping now reflects feedback from the Department and includes additional areas such as Arklow Town and 
Environs for the first time. All residential and mixed-use lands have been carefully reviewed to ensure accuracy and 
consistency. This work supports national housing policy and provides greater clarity for landowners and the public. 
2. Public Planning Portals and Engagement 
Several public-facing planning portals were enhanced to improve accessibility and ease of use. The “Call for Sites” and 
Variation No. 6 consultation portals allowed members of the public to view information online and make submissions in a 
clear and transparent way.  These digital tools continue to support open and inclusive planning processes. 
3. Interactive Mapping and Online Services 
New and improved interactive web maps were developed to support both public access and internal decision-making. 
These include planning, environmental and land-use viewers that allow users to explore locations alongside key 
constraints such as flood risk, heritage and zoning.  
4. Environmental and Biodiversity Supports 
GIS data and mapping were provided to support a range of environmental initiatives across the county. This included 
protected area mapping for the Wicklow Biodiversity Action Plan and spatial data for the Grey Squirrel Eradication 
Programme. These datasets help inform evidence-based environmental management and conservation efforts. The work 
supports national biodiversity objectives at a local level. 
5. Derelict Sites and Land Management 
Work commenced on identifying lands under the Derelict Sites Act in line with statutory requirements. Updated datasets 
are being prepared to support local and national reporting, including a proposed aggregated national derelict sites 
database. This work strengthens oversight of underutilised land and supports regeneration objectives.. 
6. Support to Infrastructure and Public Services 
Mapping and data support were provided for a range of infrastructure and public service needs, including fire hydrant 
planning, gas network updates, harbour CCTV locations and port signage. Accurate spatial data helps ensure services 
are delivered efficiently and safely.
